newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon to get IMF loan August 20-minister.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon to get IMF loan August 20-minister.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund is expected to sign a formal agreement on an Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility with Cameroon on August 20, Cameroon's Finance Minister Edouard Akame Mfoumou said on Friday.
The government announced on Thursday it had signed a letter of intent with the IMF.

"The effects of signing the letter of intent are immediate, since within a fortnight the World Bank will release $125 million and France 20 billion CFA francs ($32 million)) for Cameroon," Mfoumou said.
"On the signing of the confirmation agreement, the IMF will release 22 billion CFA francs ($36 million)," he added.

The ESAF agreement, Cameroon's first, will run for three years until 2000. Cameroon has had four shorter stand-by arrangements with the IMF in the past but they have all fallen through because agreed policies were not maintained. ($ = 615 CFA francs)
